formats.key: mintToken(uint256 eventId, uint256 tokenId, address receiver, uint256 expirationTime, bytes signature)
effects: The signer sends all of msg.value in ETH to the bridge's feeReceiver (read from storage). msg.value must be at least migrationFee, and any extra is kept, not refunded.
POAP token `tokenId` of event `eventId` is minted by the POAP contract to `receiver`, who may not be the signer.
The off-chain mint signature is marked as used, so it cannot be replayed. The call reverts once block.timestamp reaches `expirationTime`.
formats.shown: "Mint POAP" with the token id (raw), the receiver, an 'Expiration Time' date and the ETH sent as 'Migration Fee'. The event id and signature are hidden.

findings.title: mintToken: 'Expiration Time' is when the mint authorization expires, not when the POAP expires.
findings.evidence: PoapBridge.sol mintToken: `require(block.timestamp < expirationTime, "Signature expired");`. The value is only used as the signature deadline. descriptor: label "Expiration Time" on #.expirationTime. Case 0 shows 'Expiration Time 2026-01-09 14:27:15Z', which reads as if the minted token stops being valid at that time.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Mint valid until" or "Signature expires".

findings.title: mintToken: eventId, which tells which event's POAP is minted, is hidden with visible: never.
findings.evidence: descriptor: {"label":"Event Id","path":"#.eventId","visible":"never"}. PoapBridge.sol mintToken: `return POAPToken.mintToken(eventId, tokenId, receiver);`. The event id decides which POAP collection the minted token belongs to. Case 0 has eventId 553 (0x229), and it is not on screen.
findings.fix: Make #.eventId visible as 'Event' (raw) so the signer can check which event's POAP is being minted.

findings.title: mintToken: the intent 'Mint POAP' leaves out the receiver and the ETH paid. There is no interpolatedIntent.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "intent": "Mint POAP", no interpolatedIntent. PoapBridge.sol mintToken: `feeReceiver.transfer(msg.value);` and the mint goes to `receiver`, which can be a third party.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Mint POAP #{tokenId} to {receiver} for {@.value}".

findings.title: mintToken: the ETH goes to feeReceiver, which comes from storage and cannot be shown. Overpayment is not refunded.
findings.evidence: PoapBridge.sol mintToken: `require(msg.value >= migrationFee, ...); feeReceiver.transfer(msg.value);`. feeReceiver and migrationFee are storage values (constructor fee 0.1 ETH). The full @.value is shown as 'Migration Fee', so the amount that leaves is stated.
findings.fix: None needed beyond the @.value field. A label like 'ETH paid (fee)' could make clear that the whole value is taken.

findings.title: mintToken: the only test case sends 0 ETH, so the fee field is never shown with a non-zero amount.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: input.value "0", screen 'Migration Fee: 0 ETH'. The constructor set migrationFee to 100000000000000000 wei. Unless the fee was later lowered, this call would revert with 'Insufficient payment'.
findings.fix: Add a case with a value of at least migrationFee, for example 0.1 ETH.

couldNotCheck: The POAP token contract 0x22C1f6050E56d2876009903609a2cC3fEf83B415, which PoapBridge.mintToken calls to mint the NFT to the receiver, has no source in the directory. How it mints the token was not verified.

mintToken(uint256 eventId, uint256 token.worst: mintToken: eventId, which tells which event's POAP is minted, is hidden with visible: never.

summary.worst: mintToken: eventId, which tells which event's POAP is minted, is hidden with visible: never.
